gobkit-free.name: Gobkit free assets

resale_as_is.note: The creator dedicates the free assets to CC0 1.0, allowing redistribution and standalone resale.

asset_notes: Original free low-poly models; animation uses one continuous track. Upstream describes frame ranges at 24 fps: idle 0–29, attack 30–59, dead 60–89, walk 90–119. The dead segment should not loop. Playback and loop boundaries require engine-specific setup.
caveats: The repository provides only the first releases, not the separate named clips mentioned on the live service.
Check each asset and motion before publication; trademark and other third-party rights are not waived by CC0.

grab3d.name: Grab3D

resale_as_is.note: The license page explicitly allows redistributing the models, original or modified, and explicitly allows reselling the models themselves.

asset_notes: AI-assisted origin disclosed by the provider; some storefronts require an AI content disclosure.
caveats: Every download package ships its own LICENSE.txt and manifest.json, and the adapter verifies both before fetching the model. No attribution, account or fee is required, and the license file does not have to ship with your product.
Grab3D waives only its own rights. Subjects are described as generic, with no brands, logos or real people.
The Grab3D name may not be used to imply endorsement.

Models generally start as an AI image-to-3D draft that is then cleaned up, scaled, textured and checked in Blender; rigged packages add an auto-generated skeleton and clips. This is recorded per asset as origin.ai_content and the ai-assisted tag.

kenney.name: Kenney

resale_as_is.note: The CC0 dedication places no restriction on resale, and the creator has publicly confirmed that as-is resale is permitted. Editorial note from this library, not a creator request and not a licence condition: repackaging a free pack as a paid product is a poor way to treat a creator who released it for free.

asset_notes: Third-party GLB conversion of a Kenney pack; conversion and embedded textures are also CC0.
caveats: The standalone page https://kenney.nl/license returned 404 when checked on 2026-11-04. The evidence used instead is the support page (all asset-page assets are CC0, attribution not required) plus the license file pinned in the exact source revision each asset came from.
Kenney reserves its studio logo for official projects. The logo is not part of any asset here and must not be used to imply endorsement.

Files come from a pinned third-party mirror that converts Kenney's packs to GLB. That mirror's license explicitly releases its conversions, embedded textures and thumbnails under CC0 as well. Kenney remains the original creator and is recorded as such.

makehuman-clothing.name: MakeHuman Community clothing packs

resale_as_is.note: CC0 places no copyright restriction on redistribution or sale.

asset_notes: Only individually indexed CC0 garments from pinned community packs are used; creator and per-pack row are recorded per asset.
caveats: The MakeHuman asset pack index separates CC0 packs from CC-BY packs; only individually indexed CC0 garments are eligible.
A descriptor explicitly naming a non-CC0 license conflicts with the index and is rejected pending clarification.
The OBJ converter recreates diffuse and declared normal textures; other legacy shader maps and rigging are not reproduced.

modkit-industrial.name: ModKit by Jaron Bragg

resale_as_is.note: The pinned README dedicates meshes and the assembled example to CC0 1.0; CC0 permits redistribution and resale of the files themselves.

asset_notes: Procedural industrial kit; materials are untextured and should not be presented as photorealistic PBR.
caveats: The example scene and individual components are from the same pinned upstream repository. Confirm in-engine navigation, collisions, scale and visual quality before assuming it is a complete playable map.
CC0 does not clear trademarks, patents or third-party rights; inspect all models and source evidence individually.

oga-submersible.name: weirdybeardyman Yellow Submersible on OpenGameArt

resale_as_is.note: The individual contributor page marks the model CC0, which permits standalone redistribution and sale.

asset_notes: Only the individually reviewed Yellow Submersible is covered by this entry.
caveats: Page license evidence is not independent proof of authorship or third-party rights.
Blender conversion and actual appearance require review.

polyhaven.name: Poly Haven

resale_as_is.note: The license page states the assets can be redistributed, including inside a product you sell.

caveats: Only the assets are CC0. Site content such as the Poly Haven logo, staff avatars, example renders and page text stays protected, so this library renders its own previews instead of copying promotional imagery.

Using the live discovery API is covered by separate API terms. They ask for a visible 'Powered by Poly Haven' service credit in software that calls the API. The same terms state explicitly that downloaded or self-hosted CC0 assets carry no attribution requirement whatsoever; this gallery serves local files and keeps the credit as a courtesy.
A few Poly Haven assets carry a trademark warning flag in their API metadata. None of the approved assets in this library carry that flag; each asset stores the API metadata it was selected from.

research-vintage.name: piopis vintage car via Bitterli and glTF Research Scenes

resale_as_is.note: The car scene is CC0; the original environment map is separately restricted and excluded.

asset_notes: Restricted to piopis vintage car; no original HDR environment included.
caveats: CC0 documentation does not independently verify authorship or third-party rights.
The conversion is approximate and the floor and camera were removed from the active scene.

universal_caveats: An author's stated request is honoured even where CC0 would legally allow more. A source whose creator asks that copies not be redistributed or resold is not accepted, and any already-published asset from such a source is retired. KayKit was withdrawn on exactly this basis.
CC0 waives copyright and related rights. It does not waive trademark or patent rights, and it does not clear rights a third party may hold in a depicted subject.
CC0 offers no warranty. The library's own technical and visual checks are the quality guarantee, not the license.
Nothing here is exclusive. The same files are available to everyone else under the same terms.

A provider can change future terms, but a CC0 dedication already applied to a published work is irrevocable. Every asset folder keeps the license text and evidence URL that applied at acquisition time.
Storefronts have their own submission rules. AI-assisted assets may need a content disclosure (for example on Steam) even though the license permits the use.
